function: Federated multi-agent Q-learning (FMARL) jointly adapting UAV positions and RIS phase shifts to maximize SINR and energy efficiency while suppressing GaN-amplifier EMI (p. 6).
system: 5 UAV relays, 128-element reflecting RIS, 20 ground users; antenna counts not stated; NLoS scenario; 2.4 GHz, 20 MHz (pp. 3, 5).
method: Federated multi-agent reinforcement learning: per-UAV and per-RIS local Q-networks trained on-device, periodic weight aggregation at a server (every 10 episodes); reward combines SINR, energy, and EMI (pp. 6-7).
data_channel: Custom simulator: 3D scene with distance-based EMI power-law model and unspecified channel gains; urban, suburban, rural scenarios; no standardized model, dataset, or measurement (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Convergence shown per scenario (urban, suburban, rural); sweeps of user count (10-30) and time-varying EMI and density (Fig. 13); no stated train and test separation (pp. 7-13).
baselines: No-suppression, AFS-only, DSR-only; cited works [1]-[3], [5]-[7] with no joint EMI-aware design; non-federated DRL, independent and centralized MARL (variants of the proposed method) (pp. 7-8).
metrics: SINR (dB), energy efficiency (Mbps/W), EMI reduction (%), latency (ms), throughput, BER, SINR variance, convergence episodes, communication overhead (pp. 7-13).
complexity: Table VII: time complexity O(|S||A|B) for the local Q-network update, O(NxK) for DSR, total O(|S||A|B+NK) per episode; 0.40 s wall-clock per training episode (pp. 8-9).
q1_support: p. 4: "is modeled in the simulation environment" - custom 3D simulator with a distance-based EMI power law (Eq. 2); no standardized channel model, and measured GaN EMI figures from [14], [17] only sanity-check P_EMI.
q2_support: p. 7: "The FMARL training process demonstrates stable convergence behavior across all evaluated scenarios" - convergence is reported per scenario; the user-count sweep (Table X, p. 10) and Fig. 13 (p. 13) do not say the policy was trained on other conditions.
q3_support: p. 7: "(iii) a non-federated deep reinforcement learning (DRL) baseline" - the learned comparators (non-federated DRL, independent and centralized MARL, Table V) are the proposed method trained another way; cited works [1]-[3], [5]-[7] are not described as learned.
q4_support: p. 8: "Table VII Presents the computational complexity analysis of" each HESAF component - O(.) time and space per component, total O(|S||A|B+NK) per episode, and about 0.40 s wall-clock per training episode (p. 9).
q5_support: p. 4: "we compare the simulated EMI power levels with" experimentally reported GaN values - measured data only sanity-check P_EMI; the channels are simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included, area 6 by the tie-break order (aerial UAV-RIS link); the learned decisions are UAV position changes and RIS phase shifts (p. 6), so area 3 also fits and the reviewer may confirm. AFS, DSR and SPAF are formulas or argmax rules, not learned. Federated aggregation is digital over the backhaul (p. 7), so area 7 does not apply. The learned comparators are variants of the proposed method (q3 = 0). Scalability claims (Table X, Fig. 13) give no train and test separation (q2 = 0).
